title: Designing Secure Space Systems
problem: Space systems increasingly rely on commercial off-the-shelf hardware and software to accelerate development and reduce costs, but COTS components introduce vulnerabilities and expand the attack surface, creating cybersecurity risks for critical space assets.
motivation: Space exploration commercialization and militarization create high-value targets; reliance on COTS components broadens threats while traditional space system design lacks integrated cybersecurity practices.
method: The paper outlines a complete approach to building secure space systems by thinking about cybersecurity from the very start of development, not adding it at the end. It covers secure design practices (building security into how the system is built), thorough testing to find vulnerabilities, strategies to keep systems working even under attack, and industry standards. By weaving cybersecurity into every phase—from figuring out what the system needs to do, through design, testing, and deployment—it prevents security problems from being overlooked.
key_novelty: The key idea is treating cybersecurity as integral to every stage of space system development, from requirements to deployment, rather than as an afterthought.
contributions: Framework for integrating cybersecurity throughout space system lifecycle
Secure engineering practices adapted for space asset development
Comprehensive testing and validation methodologies for space security
Cyber resiliency strategies for operational space systems
Role of standardization in enabling consistent security posture
limitations: Specific technical contributions and threat models not detailed; primarily survey and framework paper.
